title: OAuth 2.0

searches.query: "OAuth 2.0" interview PKCE redirect URI public client
searches.result: success; exact-concept search executed, but independent frequency/rank/company evidence was insufficient; prompts are original production adaptations and technical decisions use checked primary sources

sources.title: System Design Primer: Security
sources.supportRationale: Core conceptual orientation checked during specification; its brief section explicitly needs updates and is not the sole protocol/crypto authority or evidence of interview frequency.

sources.title: IETF RFC 6749: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework
sources.supportRationale: OAuth roles, authorization-code exchange and access/refresh token responsibilities, read with current security BCPs rather than obsolete defaults.

sources.title: IETF RFC 9700: OAuth 2.0 Security Best Current Practice
sources.supportRationale: Modern OAuth threat model, redirects, PKCE, client-specific refresh-token replay protection and scoped revocation concerns.

sources.title: IETF RFC 7636: Proof Key for Code Exchange
sources.supportRationale: Per-authorization-request verifier/challenge binding and supported exchange validation; distinct from arbitrary API proof of possession.

sources.title: IETF RFC 10017: OAuth 2.0 for Browser-Based Applications
sources.supportRationale: Browser OAuth threats and architectural boundaries including BFFs, checked as the published August 2026 BCP rather than an old draft.

sources.title: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 incorporating errata set 2
sources.supportRationale: Identity layer, ID Token and flow-specific issuer/audience/nonce validation; logout/discovery details need their own verified extension contract if used.

sources.title: OWASP: Authorization Cheat Sheet
sources.supportRationale: Least privilege, default denial and resource/action authorization on every request, with trusted enforcement and failure handling.

sources.title: OWASP: REST Security Cheat Sheet
sources.supportRationale: API credentials, token/access controls, safe error/log handling and TLS; API keys alone are insufficient for every sensitive resource.

sources.title: IETF RFC 8725: JSON Web Token Best Current Practices
sources.supportRationale: Algorithm verification, trusted keys, issuer/audience and distinct JWT usage profiles; not a universal authorization or revocation protocol.

scenarios.theme: A calendar access token is used as the app’s user identity. What is missing?
scenarios.assumptions: The client has delegated resource access but no verified end-user identity assertion contract. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A calendar access token is used as the app’s user identity. What is missing?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Use OIDC or another supported authentication protocol for identity, validate its assertions and keep calendar authorization separately scoped.

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Another protocol adds configuration

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: An access token may enable a profile API under a defined contract, but its existence alone is not a universal login statement.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to oauth, oidc; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: An authorization redirect can forward to an arbitrary URL. What do you fix?
scenarios.assumptions: A registered endpoint acts as an open redirector and can leak authorization responses. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: An authorization redirect can forward to an arbitrary URL. What do you fix?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.
